project: Evaluating generalization of ML for SOC prediction in China under spatial and depth constraints

missing_value_policy.BD_g_cm3: impute with median (only 13.5% missing, co-occurs with SOC missing)

primary.name: Spatial Block CV (5°×5° grid)
primary.description: Each fold holds out ~20% of 5°×5° grid cells; prevents spatial data leakage

baseline.name: Random 5-Fold CV
baseline.description: Standard random CV as lower-bound comparison; expected to overestimate

Mean_baseline.description: Predict training set mean; sanity check

analysis_dimensions: Delta R² by model and depth

hypotheses.H1: Random CV overestimates SOC prediction accuracy compared to spatial block CV (ΔR² > 0)
hypotheses.H2: SOC predictability decreases systematically with depth
hypotheses.H3: The overestimation from random CV is larger for tree-based models than linear models
hypotheses.H4: The overestimation from random CV is larger for deep soil than surface soil

stopping_rules.description: No formal early stopping; all models trained to completion for each seed

tables: results/delta_r2_analysis.csv — ΔR² by model and depth
results/source_data/fig3_performance.csv — source data for main results figure
figures: fig1: Study area map with sampling points and climate zones
fig2: Data overview (depth distribution, SOC distribution, land cover)
fig3: Model performance comparison (random vs spatial, by depth)
fig4: Spatial block degradation map (ΔR² spatial distribution)
fig6: Covariate importance by depth (SHAP or permutation)

notes: Pilot used 20% subsample (1175 profiles, 4035 samples); formal uses all 5877 usable profiles
XGBoost and sklearn RF require installation; pure numpy fallback available
Hyperparameter tuning to be done on 20% validation subset before full training
SHA-256 checksums to be computed and recorded before full training
